subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy, audit, inventory, and Gateway consumers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines public SDK/Gateway security facts and must coordinate with overlapping provenance, capability-grant, classification, audit, and Security Matrix work.

options.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through SDK, hooks, trusted policies, inventories, Gateway protocol, docs, and tests, and document that declarations do not grant authorization.

options.title: Fold into capability permissions
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the broader capability grant/default-deny model so descriptors ship only with enforceable grants and operator consent semantics.

options.title: Limit to audit or Security Matrix first
options.body: Use an audit-only or Security Matrix consumer to settle vocabulary before exposing a general-purpose public tool descriptor field.

recommendation.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through SDK, hooks, trusted policies, inventories, Gateway protocol, docs, and tests, and document that declarations do not grant authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent host-hook/trusted-policy and plugin metadata seams that would carry this public contract.
